claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: joint-space narrowing + osteophytes + sclerosis + cysts on joint X-ray → osteoarthritis
claims.quote: Joint-space narrowing + osteophytes + sclerosis + cysts Joint X-ray Osteoarthritis

claims.text: Radiographs generally reveal marginal osteophytes, narrowing of the joint space, increased density of the subchondral bone, subchondral cyst formation, bony remodeling, and sometimes joint effusions
claims.quote: Radiographs generally reveal marginal osteophytes, narrowing of the joint space, increased density of the subchondral bone, subchondral cyst formation, bony remodeling, and sometimes joint effusions.

claims.text: Standing weight-bearing Merchant view (tangential view with knee flexed 30°) radiographs of the knees are more sensitive in detecting joint space narrowing; discrepancy between severity of symptoms and severity of imaging changes is common
claims.quote: Standing weight-bearing Merchant view (tangential view with knee flexed 30°) radiographs of the knees are more sensitive in detecting joint space narrowing. Discrepancy between severity of symptoms and severity of changes in imaging is common (1).

claims.text: Example standing knee radiograph: narrow tibiofemoral joint space in the medial compartment of both knees, particularly on the left; marginal osteophytes; attrition of the left medial tibial plateau
claims.quote: This radiograph, taken while the patient is standing, shows that the tibiofemoral joint space in the medial compartment of both knees is narrow, particularly on the left. Marginal osteophytes are visible. There is attrition of the left medial tibial plateau.
claims.locator: Radiograph of the Knee in Osteoarthritis image caption

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Labs are normal in osteoarthritis (occasionally needed to exclude other disorders or diagnose a cause of secondary osteoarthritis); synovial fluid is usually clear, viscous, and has ≤ 2000 WBC/mcL
claims.quote: Laboratory studies are normal in osteoarthritis but occasionally may be required to exclude other disorders or to diagnose an underlying disorder causing secondary osteoarthritis. If osteoarthritis causes joint effusions, synovial fluid analysis can help differentiate it from inflammatory arthritides; in osteoarthritis, synovial fluid is usually clear, viscous, and has ≤ 2000 WBC/mcL.

claims.text: Causes A chronic arthropathy with progressive loss of joint cartilage plus other joint changes, including bone hypertrophy (periarticular osteophyte formation and sclerosis)
claims.quote: Osteoarthritis is a chronic arthropathy characterized by progressive loss of joint cartilage along with other joint changes, including bone hypertrophy (periarticular osteophyte formation and sclerosis).

claims.text: Mechanism of the X-ray findings: subchondral bone stiffens, then undergoes infarction, and develops subchondral cysts; attempts at bony repair cause subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes at the joint margins
claims.quote: Subchondral bone stiffens, then undergoes infarction, and develops subchondral cysts. Attempts at bony repair cause subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes at the joint margins.

claims.text: Trigger is most often unknown, but sometimes begins with abnormal mechanics from an injury (eg, torn meniscus), transmission of inflammatory mediators from the synovium into cartilage, or defects in cartilage metabolism
claims.quote: The trigger of osteoarthritis is most often unknown, but osteoarthritis sometimes begins with abnormal mechanics from an injury (eg, torn meniscus), transmission of inflammatory mediators from the synovium into cartilage, or defects in cartilage metabolism.

claims.text: Secondary osteoarthritis: significant trauma, congenital joint abnormalities, metabolic defects (eg, hemochromatosis, Wilson disease), infections, endocrine and neuropathic diseases, and disorders that alter hyaline cartilage (eg, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, calcium crystal deposition disease)
claims.quote: Secondary osteoarthritis results from conditions that change the microenvironment of the cartilage or joint structure. These conditions include significant trauma, congenital joint abnormalities, metabolic defects (eg, hemochromatosis, Wilson disease), infections (causing postinfectious arthritis), endocrine and neuropathic diseases, and disorders that alter the normal structure and function of hyaline cartilage (eg, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, calcium crystal deposition disease).

claims.text: Symptoms Onset is most often gradual, usually beginning with 1 or a few joints
claims.quote: Onset of osteoarthritis is most often gradual, usually beginning with 1 or a few joints.

claims.text: Pain is the earliest symptom, sometimes described as a deep ache; usually worsened by weight bearing and relieved by rest, but can eventually become constant
claims.quote: Pain is the earliest symptom of osteoarthritis, sometimes described as a deep ache. Pain is usually worsened by weight bearing and relieved by rest but can eventually become constant.

claims.text: Stiffness after awakening or inactivity generally lasts < 30 minutes and lessens with movement; as it progresses, joint motion becomes restricted and tenderness and crepitus develop; joint effusions are common in larger joints, particularly the knees
claims.quote: Stiffness follows awakening or inactivity but generally lasts < 30 minutes and lessens with movement. As osteoarthritis progresses, joint motion becomes restricted, and tenderness and crepitus or grating sensations develop. In larger joints, particularly the knees, joint effusions are common.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Nonpharmacologic (eg, patient education, weight loss, joint protection strategies) and pharmacologic measures (eg, topical or oral NSAIDs) for pain relief; surgical measures (eg, total joint replacement) may be required for advanced disease with inadequate symptom control
claims.quote: Treatment includes nonpharmacologic (eg, patient education, weight loss, joint protection strategies) and pharmacologic measures (eg, topical or oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDs]) for pain relief. Surgical measures (eg, total joint replacement) may be required for patients with advanced disease with inadequate symptom control.

claims.text: NSAIDs are the mainstay of pharmacologic therapy; topical medications are preferred as initial therapy for knee and hand joints; oral NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors) may be considered for refractory pain or signs of inflammation, for the shortest possible duration; gastric protection should be strongly considered with chronic NSAIDs
claims.quote: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are the mainstay of pharmacologic therapy for osteoarthritis. Topical medications are preferred as initial therapy for knee and hand joints (ie, superficial joints) given their possible efficacy and limited systemic exposure, thereby minimizing the risk of adverse drug effects (6). Oral NSAIDs, including selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitors (coxibs), may be considered if patients have refractory pain or signs of inflammation (eg, erythema, warmth); they should be used for the shortest possible duration given the risk of potential adverse gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and renal effects. Gastric protection should be strongly considered when using chronic NSAIDs.

claims.text: Laminectomy, osteotomy, and total joint replacement should be considered if nonsurgical approaches fail
claims.quote: Laminectomy, osteotomy, and total joint replacement should be considered if nonsurgical approaches fail.
